text: Assumption: Hardware crypto drivers use internal Exclusive Areas to protect accesses to hardware registers between ISR and task level — is this correct?
text_en: Assumption: Hardware crypto drivers use internal Exclusive Areas to protect accesses to hardware registers between ISR and task level — is this correct?
norm: hardware crypto drivers use internal exclusive areas to protect accesses to hardware registers between isr and task level
assumption: Hardware crypto drivers use internal Exclusive Areas to protect accesses to hardware registers between ISR and task level.
rationale: The SWS snippet for asynchronous driver processing (SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_2_2_Asynchronous_Job_Processing) specifies the decoupling of kickoff and completion, but does not name any specific exclusive area identifiers of the driver.

original.text: Annahme: Hardware-Kryptotreiber dürften interne Exclusive Areas verwenden, um Zugriffe auf Hardwareregister zwischen ISR und Task-Ebene abzusichern — trifft das zu?
original.assumption: Hardware-Kryptotreiber dürften interne Exclusive Areas verwenden, um Zugriffe auf Hardwareregister zwischen ISR und Task-Ebene abzusichern.
original.rationale: Der SWS-Ausschnitt für asynchrone Treiberverarbeitung (SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_2_2_Asynchronous_Job_Processing) spezifiziert die Entkopplung von Kick-off und Fertigstellung, nennt aber keine konkreten Exklusivbereichs-Bezeichner des Treibers.
